method: OpenAI 内置 imagegen；8 幅原创生成插画。生成后原图直接复制，HTML/CSS 排版与显示裁切；中文标题、卡面规则由 HTML 排字。

prompts.cannon:
Use case: illustration-story. Create one standalone artwork for the printed Chinese steampunk tabletop game The Dawn Raid (劫走黎明). It must visually belong to an elegant hand-painted adventure novel: oil and gouache brushwork, finely etched riveted iron and weathered brass, petroleum teal shadows, restrained amber light, natural parchment-colored highlights. Believable late-industrial airborne ships above a fog sea, no magic. Hope and an elegy for old industry, thrilling and tactile rather than sugary. Moderate print-friendly contrast with open midtones, no masses of near-black. Crisp focal silhouette, readable when printed in a small 55 x 32 mm illustration window. Landscape 16:9. Fill the picture with artwork; no border, card layout, numbers, words, letters, logos, watermarks, or rules.
Subject: a heavy brass naval cannon firing from the iron deck of a small airborne gunboat; warm muzzle flash and rolling white smoke, recoil piston and toothed traversing base visible. A huge rusted cargo airship hangs close across the gap. Camera low beside the cannon, its physical machinery dominant; distant boarding craft retreats out of the gun's arc. At most two tiny adult crew silhouettes; no portraits or gore. The image should communicate suppressive fire, weight, risk and momentum.

Subject: a barbed boarding grapnel embedded firmly in the riveted rail of an enormous old airborne cargo ship, a thick taut cable stretches diagonally across a cloud-filled gap toward a smaller boat. The cable pulls a compact boarding cradle with two adult sailors in practical dark coats and gloves. Warm brass deck lamps cut through pale smoke. Close foreground on the hook, locked metal and tense cable; the ships establish height and daring. Physical boarding, not a mystical anchor. No gore.

Subject: a fast small industrial air skiff venting a magnificent curling white-grey smoke bank from a copper pipe, slipping beneath the gunports of a massive abandoned airborne ship. Strong recognizable small-boat silhouette in three-quarter view, brass fan, exposed pipes and rudder, wisps of orange dawn. The smoke obscures distant cannon barrels but the skiff itself remains legible. Composition suggests a clever turn and escape, not a ship on fire.

Subject: one compact salvageable steam-electric furnace dynamo on an old cargo deck. The entire machine is visible, roughly barrel-sized, riveted iron body, copper heat exchanger tubes, analogue pressure gauge, tiny amber furnace aperture, short supporting feet. Folded cream canvas and restrained foggy deck background. Still-life treasure portrait with tactile detail and clear silhouette, worthy of being stolen to restart a town's machines. No giant factory and no magical power crystal.

Subject: a treasured complete nautical chart spread over a captain's oak chart table, beside two rolled charts in brass protective tubes, an antique divider, a compass and a small warm oil lamp. Drawn coastline shapes and fine plotting grids visible but NO readable letters, numbers or invented text. Cool fog and the ghost of an iron airship outside a porthole. This is the irreplaceable knowledge that can reopen distant sea routes. Main chart and brass instruments large and legible.

undefined
Subject: a small orderly cache of valuable industrial supplies inside the legendary airship's cargo hold: one open iron-banded wooden crate containing coils of copper wire, spanner tools and neatly wrapped machine fittings; a closed crate and cream canvas bundles behind it. A loading hook hangs clear overhead, warm ship lamp, mist beyond the cargo door. Centered vivid still life, valuable useful salvage rather than generic treasure gold. No letters, seals with text, weapons or magical items.

Subject: a weathered working harbor waking in the first amber light, seen from the cabin of an old airboat. Drydock crane, a partly built hull, railway station clock and modest brick workshops, two or three lamps relit along the wharf; distant grey open sea. A folded letter with no writing lies at the edge of the foreground wooden windowsill. Tiny ordinary working people, not protagonists. This picture will decorate private rebuilding commissions: a plausible place worth bringing machinery home to. Modest hope, melancholy, practical industry, no utopia or fantasy castle.
prompts.back: Use case: illustration-story. One square decorative artwork for the COMMON BACK of a home-printed steampunk tabletop card set, The Dawn Raid. Design a centered antique engraved compass-and-airship medallion, with two identical small industrial airship silhouettes arranged in rotational symmetry, one above and one below, brass compass rings and delicate nautical cablework. Precise TWO-WAY 180-degree rotationally symmetric composition; no top or bottom distinction, no words, letters, numbers, logos or watermark. The central object should be richly detailed etched linework and delicate gouache shading, steel teal and aged brass inks on light warm ivory paper, like an expensive nineteenth century mariner's certificate. Same restrained elegant industrial adventure atmosphere as an old rusted flying ship over the misty sea. Keep at least half the total area very pale; no dark full-bleed fields, no border at the image edge. Make the motif legible at 50 x 50 mm and suitable for an economical inkjet print. No card layout or text, only the symmetric ornament.
